stem: Priya adds baking soda to water at 25 °C in a steel tumbler at home. Some baking soda settles at the bottom and does not dissolve. She then heats the mixture to 55 °C while stirring with a spoon. Which row correctly predicts what happens to the undissolved baking soda and to the amount of baking soda that can dissolve at the higher temperature?

options.text: undissolved baking soda remains at the bottom; the amount that can dissolve stays the same
undissolved baking soda dissolves; more baking soda can dissolve at the higher temperature
undissolved baking soda dissolves; less baking soda can dissolve at the higher temperature
undissolved baking soda remains at the bottom; the amount that can dissolve decreases

tables: {"headers":["undissolved baking soda on heating","amount that can dissolve at higher temperature"],"rows":[["remains at the bottom","stays the same"],["dissolves on stirring","increases"],["dissolves on stirring","decreases"],["remains at the bottom","decreases"]],"row_labels":["A","B","C","D"],"caption":"","is_option_table":true}

teacher.key_rationale: Heating the baking soda and water mixture while stirring makes the undissolved solid dissolve, and raising the temperature increases the amount of baking soda that can dissolve in the water, so row B is correct. Row A is the trap for a student who drops the heating condition and assumes warming changes nothing.
